entries.title: Pending-reversal stop-tightening deployed
entries.context: demo1_m1 and demo1_m3 had no protection against a trade that shows an early warning sign (an opposing candle) before eventually hitting its full stop-loss.
entries.decision: Added logic that halves the stop distance the moment the first opposing candle appears after entry. Deployed live on both accounts at 17:19 UTC.

entries.title: ADX-momentum entry filter added
entries.context: Looking for a way to avoid entering right as momentum was already fading.
entries.decision: Required ADX to be rising versus the previous candle at the confirming candle, otherwise the entry was blocked outright. Went live 06:45 UTC on both accounts.

entries.title: ADX filter's first day: at least 3 real missed wins
entries.context: Traced the new filter's blocked signals against real forward price action on its first live day.
entries.finding: At least 3 blocked signals that day were genuine wins if taken (one ~$30 win missed entirely, price rallied ~$12 afterward with no fresh cross to re-enter on); only 1 of 4 blocked signals would have been a loss.
entries.decision: Flagged as concerning on day one, kept running to gather more data rather than reacting to a single day.

entries.title: Full 16-trade day under stop-tightening + ADX filter
entries.context: First full day of real results combining both live protections.
entries.finding: 16 trades, 9W/7L, 56.2% win rate, net +$53.70 combined. demo1_m3 (+$90.84) carried the day; demo1_m1 lost -$37.14 on a 3-loss streak.
entries.decision: Logged as baseline, no change made yet.

entries.title: Post-entry ADX-check alternative traced against real trades
entries.context: Considered a different design: let every signal enter, then exit early only if ADX is still falling on the very next candle, instead of blocking the entry up front.
entries.finding: Traced against all 16 real trades from 2026-08-26: would have saved ~$26.83 on 2 real losses caught early, but given up ~$21.22 on 1 real win cut short. Net effect roughly +$5.61 -- essentially a wash.
entries.decision: Not built. Neither the existing before-entry filter nor this alternative showed a decisive real edge.

entries.title: ADX-momentum entry filter removed
entries.context: Built a script to automatically trace every blocked signal across both real trading days, instead of hand-tracing one at a time.
entries.finding: 41 blocked signals across both accounts over 2 days: 27 would-be wins (~+$810) versus 14 would-be losses (~-$720) -- the filter cost about $90 more than it saved.
entries.decision: Removed entirely. Every confirmed cross is taken again, gated only by the gap/EMA5-pullback rule (itself later removed, see 2026-08-31 below). The stop-tightening and swap/reversal gate were unaffected.

entries.title: demo1_m3 risk:reward rebalanced 15:5 to 10:6
entries.context: The old 3:1 stop:take-profit ratio needed a 75% win rate just to break even.
entries.finding: demo1_m3's real win rate so far (87.5% across 16 trades, under the old 15:5 settings) comfortably cleared both the old and new ratios, but the new 1.67:1 ratio leaves much more room if win rate ever drops.
entries.decision: stop_loss_usd 15 to 10, take_profit_usd 5 to 6. Agreed not to judge the change on fewer than 10-15 new trades under the new settings.

entries.title: demo2 account pair built and deployed
entries.context: A second, simpler engine variant was built for a separate demo2_m1/demo2_m3 account pair -- same entry rule as demo1's engine, but deliberately without the 2-candle debounce, ADX gate, or stop-tightening demo1 has.
entries.decision: Went live 09:58 UTC under Task Scheduler supervision, entirely separate from demo1 -- created specifically to be demo1's real-data A/B comparison partner.

entries.title: Swap-ADX-threshold simulation
entries.context: Tested whether lowering the ADX >= 25 threshold gating demo1's swap/reversal mechanism would recover any real blocked trades.
entries.finding: 0 of the real blocked swaps had an actual ADX reading >= 20 -- a lower threshold would have changed nothing.
entries.decision: Threshold left at 25, no change made.

entries.title: "Force every entry through EMA5-pullback" -- tested, not deployed
entries.context: Since wide-gap/EMA5-touch entries were already known to outperform small-gap immediate entries, tested forcing every entry through the pullback rule.
entries.finding: demo1_m1 (23 samples): forced pullback would net exactly $0.00 versus real -$13.80, and 1 of 23 would have been cancelled entirely -- the exact risk flagged before testing, confirmed to actually happen. demo1_m3 (8 samples): looked strong (+$96.00 vs real +$30.48) but far too small a sample to trust -- the same size that made the ADX filter look good just before it cost $90.
entries.decision: Not deployed. Kept the existing small-gap-immediate-entry rule; planned to re-check once demo1_m3 had more samples.

entries.title: Tick volume, EMA separation, and ATR volatility filters -- checked, not pursued
entries.context: Three more candidate entry-quality filters suggested by an earlier analysis.
entries.finding: Tick volume showed a real but small effect (~4.7% of total P/L, cutting 35% of trades to get it). EMA13/21 separation was weak and noisy. ATR volatility was clean and monotonic, but the low-volatility bucket was barely breakeven, not a real loss -- nothing to reclaim.
entries.decision: None pursued as standalone rules -- all three closed out.

entries.title: Time-of-day check flags demo1_m1's 12:00-16:00 window
entries.context: Broke down every real trade into 4-hour app-time buckets.
entries.finding: demo1_m1's 12:00-16:00 window was its single biggest bucket (12 of 26 trades) and its worst -- only 33.3% win rate, -$91.20, nearly all of the account's net loss for the period. Everything else was too small a sample to trust yet.
entries.decision: Not acted on. Flagged to keep watching -- a real candidate for a targeted fix (tighter stop, or exclusion) if the pattern holds up over more trades.

entries.title: Wrong-account balance cross-talk bug fixed
entries.context: A real ~9-minute balance mismatch was traced to the MetaTrader5 package's single-global-connection limitation letting one account's data leak into another's request.
entries.decision: account_info() now verifies the connected login matches the account's own config on every call, raising an error on any mismatch.

entries.title: Order-comment-length bug fixed
entries.context: A manual test trade got stuck open after the broker rejected an order whose comment exceeded its length limit.
entries.decision: Added a hard 26-character cap with a safe-truncation helper, applied to every open/close order comment.

entries.title: demo1-vs-demo2 daily comparison log established
entries.context: With demo2 running the same entry rule but none of demo1's extra swap-side protections, this became a genuine live A/B test on the same real market.
entries.finding: Day 1: demo1's caution was a wash on M1 (avoided trades net -$11.58, near breakeven) but clearly helped on M3 (avoided trades net -$57.60).
entries.decision: Track daily going forward. Explicitly agreed not to conclude anything before 1-2 consistent weeks of data -- the ADX filter's first-day result had already been a false signal once.

entries.title: demo1_m3 gap threshold raised to $7
entries.context: User's explicit call, made despite a flagged concern that this ran against stronger existing evidence.
entries.finding: The flagged concern: only 1 trade that day was attributable to the gap-threshold difference (too small a sample), and raising the threshold pushed more trades into the weaker immediate-entry category rather than the stronger EMA5-pullback one.
entries.decision: Changed anyway per explicit user decision -- gap_threshold_usd 5 to 7 on demo1_m3 only.

entries.title: demo2_m1 stopped trading 16:00-19:00 Sri Lanka time
entries.context: User's explicit request, demo2_m1 only -- demo2_m3 explicitly excluded from the change.
entries.decision: Removed that session window entirely, confirmed live via the account's own heartbeat showing WAITING (not ACTIVE) during that window.

entries.title: Gap/EMA5-pullback rule removed on all four accounts
entries.context: Final strategy decision: every confirmed cross now enters immediately, with no gap-size branching or EMA5-pullback wait on any account.
entries.decision: gap_threshold_usd set effectively infinite on demo1_m1, demo1_m3, demo2_m1, and demo2_m3 -- the EMA5-pullback code path is now fully dormant everywhere.

entries.title: Breakeven-stop added on M1 accounts
entries.context: A trade that gets most of the way to its take-profit and then reverses was closing at a full loss instead of flat.
entries.decision: Once floating profit reaches $4.50 (90% of the $5 take-profit) on demo1_m1 or demo2_m1, the stop-loss moves to the entry price. demo1_m3/demo2_m3 explicitly untouched -- M1 only.

entries.title: Professional web dashboard built and deployed
entries.context: All of the analysis above was only ever visible by asking directly -- none of it was surfaced in the existing mobile control app.
entries.decision: Built a Flutter Web dashboard (Dashboard, Strategy Analysis, demo1-vs-demo2 comparison, plus this Strategy Overview and Research Log) reachable through the same Cloudflare Tunnel URL, while trimming the mobile app down to just the on/off control. Fixed a Cloudflare Tunnel path-scoping bug found during first deployment.

entries.title: Candle-based breakeven check confirmed working on a real trade
entries.context: Investigating why a specific real demo1_m1 trade (14:41 app time, 2026-08-31) never armed its $4.50 breakeven despite price appearing to reach the trigger on the 1-minute candle's low.
entries.finding: Replayed the real tick-by-tick bid stream for that exact trade: it genuinely never crossed $4.50 on a live tick (best real tick was $4.53 but landed on a different candle than first suspected) -- the tick-based check working exactly as designed, not a bug. Separately, checked every breakeven_armed event since deploy: all 10 on demo1_m1 and all 4 on demo2_m1 were followed by a real take-profit, never a reversal-saved-by-breakeven case yet. On 2026-09-01 the new candle-based check (added 2026-08-31) fired for real for the first time on demo1_m1 (01:04 UTC, caught via candle high/low, not the live tick poll) -- that trade also went on to hit take-profit shortly after.
entries.decision: No code change from this investigation -- confirms both the tick-based and candle-based breakeven paths are working as designed.

entries.title: Full entry-quality research: 7 real-data points checked per account
entries.context: User asked for the root causes of losses, how to reduce them, and how to confirm a "real" entry -- ran scripts/analyze_entry_quality.py and scripts/analyze_time_of_day.py across all 4 accounts (demo1_m1, demo1_m3, demo2_m1, demo2_m3), 242 real trades since 2026-08-25, then verified every pooled finding against each account individually before trusting it (the project's standing small-sample lesson).
entries.finding: Only 3 of 7 candidate signals held up per-account, not just pooled: (1) Time-of-day -- 00:00-04:00 broker/app time positive in ALL 4 accounts (strongest, most consistent finding); 08:00-12:00 broker/app time negative in 3 of 4. (2) Tick volume on the entry candle -- "busy candle wins more" held on ALL 4 accounts independently, second-strongest. (3) Candle closed in the trade's own favor (green candle for BUY, red for SELL) -- real in all 4, but the dramatic pooled effect (48.5% vs 59.4% win rate) was mostly one account's small sample (demo2_m3, only 14 trades); modest on the other 3. The other 4 candidates (EMA13/21 separation, ATR/volatility, gap size, candle decisiveness) looked clean when pooled but fell apart or reversed per account -- not real, actionable signals.
entries.decision: Did not touch demo1's or demo2's live entry rule with any of this (same discipline as the ADX-filter lesson). Instead built a brand-new dedicated test account, demo3, to test the two strongest actionable candidates (candle-color + tick-volume) live, without risking demo1/demo2's real results.

entries.title: demo3_m1/demo3_m3 built: combined entry-filter live test
entries.context: Explicit user decision: rather than leave tick volume untested (no demo4 account exists), combine the two strongest real-data findings from the entry-quality research into ONE new engine variant and test both live on the one available account, logging which specific condition blocks each skipped entry so the two rules can be told apart later from demo3's own real trade history.
entries.decision: New strategy_variant=dual_cross_confirmed_swap_adx_entryfilter (bot/strategy/state_machine_dual_cross_confirmed_swap_adx_entryfilter.py) -- identical to demo1's dual_cross_confirmed_swap_adx engine (same 2-candle+ADX swap debounce, pending-reversal stop-tightening, candle-based+tick-based breakeven) plus one addition: skip the entry unless the confirming candle closed in the trade's favor AND its tick volume is not in the bottom third of the recent distribution. demo3_m1/demo3_m3 mirror demo1_m1/demo1_m3's real current parameters exactly (same SL/TP/breakeven/sessions) for a clean A/B comparison. Verified with a real engine instance covering all 4 favor/volume combinations. Not yet deployed to the server -- still needs a new MT5 demo login installed as a terminal, .env.demo3_m1/.env.demo3_m3, and Scheduled Tasks.

entries.title: demo3 shelved -- proper backtest + shadow-logging in demo1 instead
entries.context: Rather than build the full demo3 infrastructure (new MT5 terminal, .env files, Scheduled Tasks) for an untested combined filter, ran a proper trade-by-trade backtest first (scripts/simulate_demo3_entry_filter.py, no lookahead), then added zero-risk shadow-only logging directly to demo1_m1/demo1_m3's real live engine instead of deploying demo3.
entries.finding: The backtest revealed the two filters have OPPOSITE effects per timeframe: candle-color filter +$122.58 on demo1_m1 (only skips 39% of trades) but -$41.94 on demo1_m3; tick-volume filter +$151.02 on demo1_m3 (only skips 21%) but -$59.82 on demo1_m1. Combining both (demo3's original design) nets to roughly break-even on both while skipping 46-65% of all trades -- the worst of the three options, since requiring both conditions cancels out each timeframe's own real edge with the other's harmful one.
entries.decision: demo3_m1/demo3_m3's code stays committed but is NOT deployed/running anywhere. Added non-blocking shadow fields (shadow_closed_in_favor, shadow_low_volume, shadow_tick_volume) to every real trade_entered log line on demo1_m1/demo1_m3 -- computed but never acted on, real trading unchanged. Will check after 1-2 weeks of real forward data whether shadow-flagged trades actually tended to lose, before considering any live rule change. Also caught and fixed a real bug while building this: a bare pandas .quantile() comparison returns numpy.bool_/numpy.float64, which json.dumps() cannot serialize -- would have crashed real logging in production.

entries.title: Time-of-day (Point 5) backtested and shadow-logged too
entries.context: The 00:00-04:00 broker/app-time window was the single strongest, most consistent finding of the whole research session (positive in all 4 accounts independently) but hadn't been given the same trade-by-trade rigor as the entry-quality points -- built scripts/simulate_time_of_day_window.py to fix that.
entries.finding: "Only trade the best window" is a bad idea -- cuts 82-90% of all trades and costs real money on both accounts (-$11.58 demo1_m1, -$449.70 demo1_m3). "Exclude the worst window" (08:00-12:00 broker time) is genuinely promising on demo1_m1: +$179.88, only cutting 15% of trades -- the best cost/benefit ratio found in the entire research session. On demo1_m3 it's a small cost (-$23.64, only 11 trades), and notably contradicts an earlier per-account check that had shown this window clearly negative for demo1_m3 -- the picture shifted as more real data came in.
entries.decision: Added shadow_app_hour and shadow_in_excluded_window fields to demo1_m1/demo1_m3's real trade_entered log line, same non-blocking pattern as the entry filters -- no live MT5 offset measurement needed since the candle's own timestamp is already raw broker/app time. Will re-check with real forward data before considering an actual session exclusion.
